title: PROP-114 full design + ROOT-CAUSE investigation — Fix C window blind-spot is half the story. Tinker authored PROP-114 to fix the Fix C visibility bug, but PROP-113 P3 shipped Fix A+B+C and we still see 23/day resurrection. Either (a) Fix A/B are partially working and only the visibility is broken, or (b) Fix A/B aren't fully blocking and Fix C just makes the leakage invisible. Author concrete edit-level design for the Fix C re-add-event detection (mirror PROP-113 design), AND investigate which re-add code path bypasses Fix A/B for the 23 daily leakers. Propose-only; operator reviews + selects phase to ship.
context:
PROP-113 Phase P3 shipped 2026-06-22T16:33Z (commit 4c76b43): Fix A (upper-bound trust gate) + Fix B (build-git-deleted-set.js helper) + Fix C (post-sync resurrection assertion). 24h later (2026-06-23T02:40Z tinker run, commit c2ef0f3), the PROP-099 canary fires with RC=3 resurrected_total=23 — a 93% reduction from the pre-fix 312/48h, but not zero.

Tinker authored PROP-114 explaining Fix C's blind-spot: check-prune-resurrection.js windows by TOMBSTONE mtime (line 53: `if(mt && mt < cutoff) continue`), so `--hours 2` only considers files tombstoned in the last 2 hours. The actual loop re-adds files tombstoned DAYS ago: FUSE retains the per-run JSON indefinitely (no unlink), prune deletes the git copy, and a later workspace-sync re-adds it. The RE-ADD event is fresh but the TOMBSTONE is old. Workspace-sync run report run-2026-06-22T23-10-45Z.json says `resurrection_status: 'clean'` while the SAME commit (5a20dcd) name-status shows 17 'A' narrative-cite-audit-*.json files. False assurance.

What PROP-114 captures so far:
  - The Fix C blind-spot diagnosis with evidence (commit 5a20dcd + run report at 22:09Z)
  - The proposed remedy direction: switch from tombstone-age window to re-add-event detection

What is MISSING (this directive asks tinker to author):
  - Concrete Edit-tool diffs (old_string/new_string) for the Fix C rewrite — same shape as PROP-113 amendment Q4 (assertion block + env-var pass-through + report-field).
  - Helper-script or check-prune-resurrection.js modification if needed — does Fix C's new question ("did any add in this commit match a tombstoned path?") fit in the existing script or need a sibling?
  - PROP-051-grade smoke-test procedure: exercise the false-clean shape (re-add of a days-old tombstoned file), verify the new assertion catches it, verify a known-good cycle still passes.
  - Disaster-vector analysis: what's the worst case if the new assertion fires false-positively? Could it abort the commit (it shouldn't — Fix C is post-commit). Could it write so many sentinels it floods integrity?
  - Backfill plan for the 23 already-resurrected files. PROP-113 Q8 assumed natural drain via prune; if Fix A/B aren't catching the loop, the 23 will keep reappearing. Need a parallel plan to drain.
  - PROP-113 lifecycle: does PROP-114 supersede PROP-113, or amend it? PROP-113's verification_pattern (residue=0 sustained) is failing — operator needs the relationship clear for PROP-102 auto-close graph.

ROOT-CAUSE QUESTION (the big one):
  PROP-113 P3 dropped resurrection from 312/48h to 23/48h. Fix A + Fix B should have stopped ALL of them if they work as designed:
    - Fix A (upper-bound gate): trips if GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES, fails-closed, all prune-managed integrity SKIPPED. If A trips, ZERO re-adds for prune categories.
    - Fix B (robust helper): builds a clean GIT_DELETED_SET. If B works, smart_copy's grep -qFx finds every tombstoned path and SKIPs.
  Yet 23 leak through. Options:
    (i) Fix A never trips because the set isn't actually overcounting any more — the helper produces an honest set. In that case Fix B's helper is correct but smart_copy has a separate gap.
    (ii) Fix A is misconfigured / the gate threshold is wrong and the actual upper-bound trip-condition is never met for the realistic resurrection size.
    (iii) The 23 re-adds happen via a code path that doesn't consult GIT_DELETED_SET at all (e.g. some other rescue mechanism, or a direct cp that bypasses smart_copy).
    (iv) FUSE→git race: the file is committed before the GIT_DELETED_SET build sees the latest archive append.
    (v) The resurrection commit (5a20dcd) added these files via a NEVER_PUSH-strand-rescue or universal-pusher path that the gate doesn't cover.
  Determining which is the FIRST half of this directive. The Fix C rewrite is only fully successful if root cause is understood — otherwise we're making the symptom visible without curing it.

Other-side checks the operator already considered:
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'The 93% reduction is good enough; just ship Fix C visibility and call it done.' Counter: 23/day = ~8400/year unbounded growth in monitor/integrity/. Less than the original 56K/year but still a slow leak. More importantly, residue=0 was PROP-113's verification_pattern — declaring done with 23/day failing means lying to the auto-close graph.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Tinker can't determine root cause without trying things; just ship visibility and learn from canary.' Counter: tinker has the run reports + the commit diff + the helper output for the 22:09Z run. The detective work IS in scope — read run-2026-06-22T23-10-45Z.json, check what Fix B's helper output (`paths_emitted`, `rejected`), check if smart_copy logged the SKIPs, cross-reference with commit 5a20dcd's name-status. The smoking gun is somewhere.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Maybe the 23 are a different bug, not the same loop.' Counter: PROP-099 canary uses the same scanner (check-prune-resurrection.js) and same definition. If it's a different bug, that's PROP-115 — but PROP-114 should still investigate enough to confirm it's the same loop shape.

investigation_questions: Q1 — Root cause: which code path. Read commit 5a20dcd (the 22:09Z workspace-sync that re-added 17 narrative-cite). Pull its corresponding run-2026-06-22T23-10-45Z.json and inspect: (a) what did Fix B helper emit for `paths_emitted` + `rejected`? (b) what GIT_DELETED_COUNT vs ARCHIVE_LINES? (c) did Fix A trip? (d) cross-reference the 17 added paths against the GIT_DELETED_SET that workspace-sync would have built — were they IN it or NOT IN it? Report the smoking gun.
Q2 — Hypothesis ranking. Based on Q1, rank the five hypotheses (i)-(v) from the context above by evidence weight. State which one fits best AND which the run report data cannot rule out.

Q3 — Fix C rewrite concrete diff. Replace the current Fix C `--hours 2` tombstone-age window check with a re-add-event detection. Two design candidates:
  (a) Compare the workspace-sync commit's added-paths (git diff --name-status HEAD~1) against the FRESH GIT_DELETED_SET — any A line whose path appears in the set is a same-cycle resurrection. Tombstone age irrelevant.
  (b) Extend check-prune-resurrection.js with `--by-add-event` mode that windows by re-add commit time + cross-references against archive paths.
  Recommend one with reasoning. Provide old_string/new_string in Edit-tool format. Validate against current workspace-sync.md.

Q4 — Helper script changes. If Q3 picks (b), what's the new check-prune-resurrection.js logic? Write the actual code, not pseudocode. If Q3 picks (a), confirm no helper changes are needed (the existing Fix B helper already builds the set; Fix C just queries the just-committed paths against it).

Q5 — Smoke-test procedure. Reproduce the 22:09Z false-clean scenario: (a) tombstone a file in archive; (b) make it exist in FUSE workspace; (c) trigger workspace-sync; (d) verify NEW Fix C catches the re-add (vs old Fix C reporting clean). Use the same kind of validated smoke as PROP-113 amendment (5/5 + parity).

Q6 — Disaster-vector analysis per fix. (i) Could the new Fix C false-positive abort workspace-sync? It shouldn't — it's post-commit. Confirm. (ii) Could it write so many sentinels it floods integrity? Bound the rate (max 1/run by definition). (iii) Could it interact badly with the universal-pusher rescue path (rescue legitimately re-adds runtime data files that wouldn't be in the integrity-only archive set)?

Q7 — Backfill plan. 23 files already resurrected in HEAD. PROP-113 Q8 assumed prune+sync cycle drains them, but if Fix A/B isn't actually catching them (per Q2), the natural drain won't work. Concrete options: (a) operator-side Git Data API tree-delete; (b) clone-side `git rm` + push; (c) wait for prune to re-tombstone + verify next workspace-sync (depends on Q2 result). Recommend.

Q8 — Sequence recommendation. (P1) ship Fix C rewrite only — get visibility right, accept residual; (P2) ship Fix C rewrite + targeted root-cause fix (depends on Q2); (P3) defer until root cause is settled. Frame trade-offs explicitly.

Q9 — PROP-113 lifecycle. Currently PROP-113 status is 'phase-P3-shipped'. Its verification_pattern (residue=0 from check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48 RC=0 sustained 2 days) is FAILING. Options: (a) Mark PROP-113 'partially-implemented' + transfer the residue=0 success criterion to PROP-114; (b) Re-open PROP-113 and add a follow-up amendment; (c) Annotate PROP-113 + author PROP-114 as the load-bearing fix. Recommend with PROP-102 auto-close interaction reasoning.
